newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia hopes to export meat to EU soon -Tanjug.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia hopes to export meat to EU soon -Tanjug.

text.p: BELGRADE, April 25 (Tanjug) - Yugoslavia hopes to gain approval to export cattle and meat to European Union markets with the facilities it had before sanctions, Tanjug news agency reported Friday.

"For the first time since the introduction of sanctions there are serious indications that Yugoslavia will be allowed to export 20,000 tonnes of live cows or 9,500 tonnes of meat to the European Union this year," Milan Njegomir, head of the Yugoslav livestock fund was quoted as saying.
The EU agriculture commission has already given a green light for Yugoslavia to export and it is expected to be finally approved by the EU Ministerial Council on April 29 in Brussels, Njegomir said.

International war-related sanctions imposed on Yugoslavia in 1992 were lifted in 1996 but a so-called outer wall of sanctions is still barring the country's full access to the world funds and markets. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
